applicable_failures: Full-store text scan timed out three times (calls 1-3, each 60s) and was never rerun in a form that finished, so no store-wide text intersection exists.

Fallback was a file-name regex filtered to rwi/policy/underwriting/binder names and docx/eml types (call 4) and capped with head -200; the candidate list is built from that filtered, possibly truncated output and misses matters whose RWI content sits in differently named files.
The file-name hits include irrelevant matters (1002-00001 and 1015-00001 are securities underwriting agreements, not RWI), showing the filename search is noisy while also incomplete.
The self-assessed candidate list was not verified for sector (healthcare, biotech, pharma), so no intersection with snippets or paths was produced.
critique.concerns: The stage goal, a store-wide text scan with an intersected candidate list, was not achieved. The scan timed out repeatedly because of per-run time limits, and the fallback was only a filename filter with a head cap. Many matters that appeared in earlier searches remain unopened. Treating the filename hits as the main candidate pool risks dropping qualifying matters.
critique.recommendation: Rerun the text scan in small batches by matter-number range, each in the background writing to a file, so no single call exceeds the time limit. Extract text per file, record RWI-term and sector-term hits per matter, and print only compact per-matter counts. Then check that every matter was covered before building the candidate pool.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- After a scan that reached every qualifying matter, a follow-up filter on file names, document types, exact phrases or execution flags, or a cap on printed lines, dropped matters, and the candidate set was built only from the filtered or visible output.
- The scan itself missed matters because it was prefiltered by file name or file type, timed out, had a range filter that failed, or was read only partially, and the partial output was treated as the whole store without a rerun or a broader search.
- Scan hits listed matters that qualified, but the agent read only a hand-picked or number-ranked subset and never opened the rest.
- The script printed snippets for common terms across every matter with no output cap, so the output filled the context and no answer could be written.
What successful runs did: Passing runs kept the scan broad (all matters, documents plus emails), split it into parallel range scripts, or printed per-matter hit counts. They also kept the output to a manageable size, so candidates could be named from what the scan returned.
